title: The Builder Greater Than the House
english: She rather fulfills the sacred rite, exalted and placed above according to her nature, while he is more closely united with the Father and the Holy Spirit. Thus God, having become flesh, would reasonably consider: we who confess that flesh came to be, the Word remained, and has overcome the power of death on our behalf—life by nature existing as from the Father’s life—are justified. For he who is truly God by nature and the Son Emmanuel will no less convince us, as the blessed Paul declares, that he became our apostle and high priest of confession, faithful in this role just as Moses was faithful in God’s house, yet having been deemed worthy of greater glory than Moses, because the builder of the house possesses greater honor than the house itself.

Again I am amazed by this in the mystagogue’s handling: he subtly undermines Israel, not merely turning them away from the sixth hour but also inclining them toward opposing Christ. He takes hold of the words and praises directed toward Moses, declaring them faithful while introducing them with wit, thereby exalting the surpassing greatness of our Savior. For he said Christ became an apostle and high priest and faithful in this, just as Moses himself had become, easily bearing the name of Moses and the praises upon him—having first set them before the Word—he immediately demonstrated that these things exist afterward in the glory of Christ. For he said Christ is to be honored more greatly, precisely because the builder of the house has greater honor than the house itself.

You see how the Word of God, having become flesh and taken the form of a servant, still orders the measures of our humanity and sets beyond the bounds of servitude, declaring himself the begetter of all things and, plainly, Moses, and crowning these works with the glory of his natural lordship.

For if it is true that none of the works share the same substance as their maker, how could anyone suppose that the maker would not be altogether and certainly superior in glory? The apostle and high priest of our confession bears witness that he was faithful to the one who made him, just as he himself was Moses the high priest, and has been counted worthy of greater glory by him, in proportion as the builder of the house has more honor than the house.
He adds to this, pointing to show that Jesus is God: every house is built by someone, but the one who built all things is God.
Therefore, if Christ were merely one of us, a man, it would be necessary to judge all things concerning him only by the time of his birth in the flesh.

But since he who is also among them the eldest of the ages, the Only-begotten Son, became a man in the good pleasure of God and Father, and this one has been named Christ Jesus, for this is a new name to him and to those who share in the times of the economy, and again it belongs to him, and if he became flesh who was before all time to be, it is necessary to confess to us that he is of all things.

title: The Eternal Nature and Supremacy of Christ
english: The Creator.

For there is one God, the Father, from whom all things proceed, and one Lord, Jesus Christ, through whom all things were made; and again, Jesus Christ is the same yesterday and today and forever, into the ages. How then can he be the same as he was yesterday, even though he was born in the most recent times of this age? It is because the most ancient nature of the Word of God has remained necessarily unshakeable, even during the era of the incarnation and this most recent dispensation.

Indeed, he at times used words concerning the forefather Abraham to address Israel, saying, "Your father Abraham rejoiced so that he might see my day, and he saw it and was glad" (John 8:56). But those who did not understand the mystery resting upon him—viewing him merely as a man like ourselves and nothing more—incoherently asked, "Do you not yet have fifty years, and you have seen Abraham?" (John 8:57). But he said to them, "Truly, truly, I say to you, before Abraham was, I am" (John 8:56-58). Therefore, he is the artisan and the creator of both Abraham and Moses and of all things; and it is necessary that the maker pre-announce all his own works, and that the beauty of the archetype be pre-manifested in those created according to his image.
In this way, the measure of Moses is unequally surpassed; rather, the glory of Christ will exceed all that has been called into existence.
Furthermore, by another method, the lawgiver Paul seeks to demonstrate that the word concerning these matters has become both wise and true.
For he says that Moses was faithful in all his house as a servant for the testimony of the things to be spoken, but Christ is as a Son upon his house, which is the house of whom we are.
So look, then, in order that you might assign to the blessed Moses a certain measure of that householder-like genuineness.
For they say that he is to be in the house faithful as a witness of the things to be spoken—that is, for the service of the words from God—but Christ is not so.

For He is not [found] as a faithful householder in the house, but as Son and Master over the house of the Father; that is to say, over us, the ones having been justified in faith and sanctified in the Spirit.

For Moses indeed was brought up through the shadow of the law, and the qualities of householder-like genuineness were brought to him as a prize, as God was saying to him, 'You shall stand beside him with me' (Hebrews 3:5), and he was greatly esteemed among the better ones in Christ.
For He has sat 'at the right hand of the throne of majesty in the high places' (Hebrews 1:3), and He has dwelt as Son and Lord in the house of His own Father.

For He encamps for us as God through His own Spirit, even though the all-wise Moses inhabited in nothing; for we have not become partakers of Moses, nor even of any other of the saints, but we have partaken of Christ through the Spirit and the blessing of the mystery.
For even though God says through one of the holy prophets, 'I will dwell in them and walk among them, and I will be their God, and they shall be a people to me' (Ezekiel 37:27).

title: Unity in Christ
english: Since the time had now come for this promise to be fulfilled, Christ took up his dwelling in us according to the ancient pledge, so that he might declare us to be temples of the living God—indeed, temples of himself—and might unite us to God the Father through himself.
He said to his holy apostles, 'On that day you will know that I am in my Father, and you are in me, and I am in you.' (John 14:20)
For whoever is united to the Lord becomes one spirit with him, as the Scripture declares. (1 Corinthians 6:17)

Again, committing us to God and the Father in this same way, he said, 'I do not pray for these alone, but also for all who will believe in me through their word, that they may all be one, just as you, Father, are in me and I am in you, so that they too may be one in us, in order that the world may believe that you sent me.' (John 17:20-21)
And the glory which you gave me I have given to them, that they may be one as we are one—I in them and you in me—so that they may be brought to complete unity. (John 17:22-23)

Therefore, in Christ we have obtained the blessing of unity toward God and Father, and this blessing remains firmly in us: that radiant and manifest adornment which belongs to those who preserve their boldness and the boast of their hope.
Moreover, in regard to this, they do not believe that alongside God the Father there exists another son who is distinct and merely partial, the one born of the holy virgin and made a temple.

Instead, they believe that he has come in accordance with the writings—that the Word became flesh and tabernacled among us—and that he has not ceased to be God, but that he is One Son and One Lord, Jesus Christ.
And he scrutinizes even to the point of division.
